chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If a man has a slave girl and he marries her to his owned slave, he separates them if he wishes, and joins them if he wishes.
ai.seo_question: What is the master's right regarding the marriage of a slave girl to a slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the master's unilateral right (ikhtiyar) to dissolve or maintain the marriage of a female slave he owns, even after she has been married to a male slave with his permission. In Shia jurisprudence, this reflects the distinct legal status of the slave-owner's authority over the marital bond of his female slave, distinguishing it from the mutual consent required in free marriages. The ruling underscores the economic and social dynamics of slavery in early Islamic society, where the master's property rights extended to the domestic arrangements of his slaves.
